1944.review_rationale: The extended-range pair 895.2/447.6 h (power 0.255) is four times stronger than the best primary peak (45.47/22.74 h, 0.061) and beats it in 100% of bootstraps. This holds without TESS: ground-only data give 895.2 h at 0.187 vs 0.148. Independent ground subsets agree: non-ATLAS stations give 894.8 h (0.207 vs 0.177 at 45.47 h), ATLAS o-band gives 448/457 h (0.21-0.23 vs 0.14), and the Europe/Africa group plus M22o, I41r and W68c alone give 895.2 h. The 45.47/22.74 h family is exactly the daily alias of this signal (2f differs by 1.00197 c/d, matching the spectral-window peak at 1.0019 c/d). TESS alone, observing continuously for 24 days, shows no power at 22.74 or 45.47 h (at most 0.02). The ground-only fold at 895.2 h is coherent and double-peaked across many datasets (amp about 0.3 mag), whereas 447.6 h folds into a single wave, so R1 (long period backed by several longitudes) and R2 give about 895 h. My own 200-sample night-block bootstrap keeps the 447.6 h tooth in 99% of resamplings (scatter 0.2 h), so sigma is set by P^2/(2dT) = 2.0 h.
1944.paper_note: The previously reported 45.47 h period is a daily alias of a slow-rotation signal; ground-based data from several longitudes give P = 895 +/- 2 h (about 37 d), with an adjacent cycle-count alternative near 914 h.
1944.concerns: TESS shows a strong trend and quantized magnitudes over its single 24-day visit, so the solution rests on ground-based data only. A long-period solution depends on accurate phase-curve reduction (phase angles up to 36 deg). The adjacent comb tooth (914 h) cannot be fully excluded. The Americas group alone still prefers the 22.74 h alias (2nd/1st 0.98).
1944.verify_reason: I tried to rescue the primary-range value 45.47 h and could not. (1) Ground data alone (TESS excluded) prefer 895.2/447.6 h (0.186) over 45.47/22.74 h (0.147). The preference survives three tests that would remove a phase-angle systematic. With per-dataset offsets plus a global polynomial in phase angle, or a per-dataset quadratic, the long period stays at 0.186-0.19. With separate offsets for each dataset and apparition it still gives 0.173 vs 0.137. (2) Each apparition analysed separately gives a period near 445-458 h (twice that is about 890-915 h) as its best period, with power 0.39-0.60, beating the best short period every time. In the apparitions observed from several longitudes (South Africa M22o, Chile W68, Tenerife R17w, Gaia P07G), 22.74 h is weak (0.07-0.16), so the daily alias is broken. (3) TESS is an independent test. A long-period model fitted to the ground data only, without TESS, predicts the TESS 24-day brightness trend in phase and sign (correlation +0.80 to +0.85). The ground-only 45.47 h model does not (correlation 0.16). After a cubic detrend, TESS has power 0.005 at 45.47 h. Injecting the ground-fitted 45.47 h light curve into the TESS data would give power 0.19, far above the 99.9th percentile (0.055), so TESS excludes 45.47 h at that epoch. The 45.47 h family is exactly the 1.0019 c/d window alias of the long-period signal. Its family fraction is only 0.70/0.73, so it is not a satisfactory primary-range solution, and the long-period exception in R1 applies. Under R2, 447.6 h folds into a single wave (amplitude 0.34), while 895.2 h folds into two maxima and two minima (amplitude 0.31) with equal power, so 895.2 h is adopted. My 200-sample night-block bootstrap puts 99.5% of resamplings in the 895 h tooth for all data (scatter 0.41 h) and 89% for ground only, where 10.5% fall in the 914 h tooth. The long period beats 45.47/22.74 h in 100% of all-data resamplings and 94.5% of ground-only ones. Therefore sigma_P = P^2/(2 dT) = 2.0 h. Quality stays B, not A: the neighbouring 914 h tooth is not fully excluded in ground data, the Americas group alone still ties at 22.74 h, and the TESS data are quantized.
1944.override_reason: The 895/448 h signal is four times stronger than any primary-range peak and survives phase-angle detrending tests, but the combined fold is dominated by TESS visit ramps, the periodogram near 895 h has many peaks of comparable power, and a period comparable to the length of an apparition can arise from slow non-rotational brightness changes (residual phase-curve or aspect effects) that all stations see. The 45.47 h peak is the daily alias of this long-period signal. Quality lowered from B to C.
1944.undetermined_reason: Long-period re-analysis (ls_longperiod.py, longperiod_tests.py, damit_longrange.py): the dominant signal (about 450/900 h) is reproduced by single apparitions (446-456 h), but slow per-apparition trends alone give 87 % of its periodogram power, the convex inversion prefers 923 h (and 454 h in one half), not 895 h, and the NPA damping time (about 6000 Gyr) makes tumbling likely. No rotation period is determined.
1944.quality_reason: long-period signal comparable to the apparition length; rotation not established

My checks were run in scratchpad with exact chi2 Lomb-Scargle. (1) TESS alone, which has no daily aliases: after detrending each visit, the strongest peak in 0.8-240 h is 4.1177 h (power 0.090), with its half 2.061 h second. Note for the pipeline: its single-dataset periodograms appear to use fastchi2, which I found returns power > 1 on small subsets (for example 703G gave 1.56 with fastchi2 and 0.42 with exact chi2). That probably explains why every single dataset was reported at exactly 24.044 h.

A low-frequency periodogram peaks at about 1290-1380 d (power 0.25-0.33). The 15.97 h member (near the manuscript's 15.997/15.976 h) correlates between Hawaii and Chile (r=+0.45) but not with M22o, and it vanishes with the rest of the comb. No alternative is better supported, so the bootstrap-preferred, double-peaked 47.94 h is kept as a nominal value at quality C. Sigma is the scatter over all teeth (0.046 h).

The family's bootstrap fraction is 1.00 in both periodograms, same tooth 0.97. TESS alone (5.091 h) and the good-quality single datasets from several longitudes (T08o, T05o, W68o, M22o, 703G, I41r) support it. The americas group and the ground-only data tie with the 1 c/d alias 2.301/4.602 h in the unweighted periodogram, so the quality is B. sigma is the resolution limit P^2/(2dT) = 0.000053 h.
4761.paper_note: The noise-weighted periodogram and TESS resolve the 1 c/d alias (4.602 h) that the unweighted ground-based data alone cannot exclude.
4761.concerns: The alias is driven by noisy LINEAR (704V) and Catalina (703V) data. TESS supplies 64 % of the points.
